newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine Avtozaz and GM sign investment study.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine Avtozaz and GM sign investment study.

text.p: General Motors and Ukraine's AvtoZAZ car maker agreed on Thursday to conduct a $500,000 study to evaluate whether they could form a joint venture.

"We have to see if we can agree on products that can be manufactured in Ukraine, and evaluate with regard to the facilities that AvtoZAZ has today and how they can be jointly utilised," Louis Sande, GM's overseas vice president, said at a signing ceremony.
The carmaker, located in the eastern industrial city of Zaporizhia, has been seeking foreign investment for the state-owned company since the start of the year.
The study would look into joint car and light truck manufacture. AvtoZAZ builds the Tavria, a mid-range car.
The study, funded in part by the U.S. government, would be completed by the end of the year, said Sande.
He declined to say how much GM would be prepared to invest.

Deputy director Mykola Lastowecky said it was not clear what share of the company could be purchased by a foreign investor. "This is still under discussion and depends on investors' interests," Lastowecky said.
Earlier in the year the government had said a majority stake in AvtoZAZ was available to investors but more recent media reports say the figure was reduced to 30 percent.
The company is one of 208 state enterprises that Ukraine's State Property Fund has made available for strategic foreign or domestic investment.
The Daewoo Group had also expressed interest in the Ukrainian car builder, and Lastowecky said AvtoZAZ was courting the South Korean company as well.
"AvtoZAZ is not just working with General Motors. AvtoZAZ is looking for foreign investors," he said.
